newsitem.title: SPAIN: FORECAST - Spain's November CPI to extend downtrend.
newsitem.headline: FORECAST - Spain's November CPI to extend downtrend.

text.p: Spain's inflation rate should continue to decline in November, slipping to 3.3 percent from 3.5 percent in October and paving the way for a seventh Bank of Spain interest rate cut this year, analysts said on Wednesday.

The Consumer Price Index (CPI), due for release on Friday, is forecast to rise 0.0-0.2 percent month-on-month for a 3.2 to 3.4 percent year-on-year increase, according to a Reuter survey of economists.
Core inflation, excluding volatile prices of fresh food and energy, is seen up 0.0-0.2 percent on the month, the poll showed
Analysts agreed that fresh food prices should continue to decline while energy prices might still be a sticking point.
"Energy prices have only recently started to fall, so this could have an effect on the data," said Marisol Fernandez at Analistas Financieros Internacionales (AFI).
But she predicted the CPI data would show lower food prices and a benign trend on the supply side on the economy.
"I'd highlight the favourable performance of non-energy industrial components, and that of fresh foods, which could begin to fall further because of the evolution of olive oil prices," she added.
The price of olive oil has fallen sharply this year as bumper harvests followed the end of a prolonged drought.
A better trend in energy prices should start to impact the consumer price index in coming months, Fernandez said.
"We can't really expect energy prices to start increasing more, or at least, we'll see lower increases in this component until the middle of the year," Fernandez said.

Juan Antonio Mielgo at Bank of America in Madrid agreed. "On the general inflation side, fresh food will improve and energy will be slightly worse, but perhaps to a lesser extent than in previous months," he said.
On core inflation, Mielgo also considered the processed food component would improve.
A recent rise in cigarette prices, passed on by tobacco firms after the government hiked "sin taxes" in July, would have a limited impact on the CPI, analysts said.
"The cigarette price rise will be reflected in December and is about the equivalent of one-tenth of one percent, so it won't be very significant," said BoA's Mielgo.
Moreover, most economists think lower inflation will prompt the Bank of Spain to cut key money rates,possibly when inflation data are released on December 13, or maybe on December 24.
